column1: # lib/recording-sources.tsv — the recording apps Old Recordings knows, and how each is treated.
# ONE list, read by both sides: the engine (storage-analyzer/cleanup.sh, recordings mode) takes each source's
# layout, extensions, keep rule and warning from here, and the app (RecordingSourceCatalog) takes the rest:
# where to look, whether it is offered, and its words. `agent-runner --probe-recording-sources` fails if the
# two sides ever read a line differently. Only the APP discovers where a source is; the engine is told the
# path (ANALYZERS_RECORDING_SOURCES in config.local.sh) and never looks for one.
# Adding a recording app is one line here, and needs no code unless it needs a new layout.
# Columns, separated by TABS (an empty column is a single "-"):
#   id <TAB> title <TAB> symbol <TAB> layout <TAB> extensions <TAB> keepIf <TAB> offer <TAB> findBy <TAB> warning
#   title       what a person sees (the app checks it against its own name table)
#   symbol      an SF Symbol name
#   layout      what ONE item is:
#     folders         each subfolder, one level down; old = nothing inside written in N days
#     meetingFolders  each subfolder that has Zoom's signature (recording.conf, a video*.mp4 + audio*.m4a pair,
#                     or a *.zoom file), plus loose files at the top with one of the extensions
#     files           each file at the top level with one of the extensions (comma list, no dots)
#     -               nothing is ever removed from this source
#   keepIf      zoomFile: a folder holding a *.zoom file is kept even when old (not converted yet); - none
#   offer       on | offWithWarning (found, switched off, with its warning) | notOffered (shown with the reason)
#   findBy      how the app finds it, one or more steps separated by | (the first that exists wins):
#     defaults:<domain>:<key>:<suffix>   a path stored in the app's own preference, plus the suffix
#     screencapture                      the Screenshot app's location-screenrecording, then location, then Desktop
#     home:<path>  documents:<path>  movies:<path>   a folder under the home, Documents or Movies; a step ending @<App>
#                                        only counts when <App>.app is installed (so a person who never used Zoom is not asked about its folder)
#     app:<Name>                         the app <Name>.app is installed (nothing inside it is opened)
#     cloudstorage                       a mount's NAME under ~/Library/CloudStorage (never opened)
#     always                             present on every Mac
#     -                                  added by the person
#   warning     for offWithWarning the sentence shown; for notOffered the reason; - none

column9: SuperWhisper keeps a history of each recording. Removing old ones here leaves entries without audio. SuperWhisper's own Keep Recordings For setting does this inside the app.

column1: loomTemporary
column9: These are videos Loom has not finished uploading. A folder here can be the only copy of a video, so look before you remove one.

column1: voiceMemos
column9: Voice Memos keeps a library synced with iCloud. Removing its files breaks the library and deletes the recordings on your iPhone, so they are never offered here.

column1: cloudMeetings
column9: These recordings live in OneDrive or Google Drive. Moving one to the Trash deletes it in the cloud, so they are never offered here.

column1: macwhisper
column9: MacWhisper keeps a database of transcripts that point at its media. Removing media behind its back leaves transcripts without audio, so use MacWhisper itself.

column1: rewind
column9: Rewind's library is its database. Removing pieces of it breaks it, so it is never offered here.

column1: granola
column9: Granola does not keep audio on your Mac, so there is nothing to remove here.

column1: wisprFlow
column9: Wispr Flow does not keep audio on your Mac, so there is nothing to remove here.
